procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory through its Factory Registration service, which requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added; registration takes about three working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately in its own right, and the authority may ask for detailed cost sheets and conduct a factory visit.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the Certificate of Origin for India e-service; the applicant logs in to the ministry e-services portal, chooses the Certificate of Origin for India service, fills in the application form, uploads the required documents, and submits the application.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for this shipment (invoice value up to AED 100,000).

The competent authority issues the certificate prior to, at, or within five working days of export, or retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment with 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9; the certificate is valid for 12 months from issue and covers only one import.

The exporter ensures the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; if in transit, under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, or storage; if third-party invoicing is used, the exporter indicates it.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020 including which origin criterion is claimed, and keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing; the importer must answer a customs request within 10 working days.

The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the year of the certificate's issue; any failure to consent to a verification visit is grounds for denying preferential benefits.

caveats.note: India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so the duty saving estimate based on the shipment value given may differ from the actual amount.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Final manufacture in the UAE and the operations beyond minimal requirements are based on the exporter's own declaration.
Mansha interprets '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.

'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement, and it is unclear whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The certificate form's box for remarks is box 9 in India's form, not box 8 as the agreement says; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a 3-year record-keeping minimum, but the CEPA requires 5 years for CEPA claims.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is confirmed only through secondary sources, not the official text.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically; the India-specific certificate page is still on the Ministry of Economy and Tourism website.
